answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with escalating proof of useful work: the first identity costs one verified task, the second two, the tenth a hundred — like a canyon that widens with every crossing. Each task must be genuinely useful, such as fact-checking or labeling data, so a fake army cannot be spun up cheaply on an isolated island of idle compute. Every identity's work history is public, so a brand-new account weighs no more than a shard of shale, while agents with long proven output carry real influence. An attacker's bill grows faster than their army.
